newsitem.title: USA: Clinton seeks $2 billion in flood, disaster aid.
newsitem.headline: Clinton seeks $2 billion in flood, disaster aid.

text.p: President Clinton asked Congress Wednesday for $2 billion in aid for a host of recent natural disasters, including floods in the Midwest, tornadoes in the South and severe winter weather in the West.

"The president's request comes after he, the vice president, and other senior administration officials visited hard-hit areas from this month's flooding and pledged a speedy federal response," a White House statement said.

Clinton requested emergency funding for the departments of agriculture, commerce, interior and transportation, plus the Army Corps of Engineers and Federal Emergency Management Agency. Congress will have to approve the requests before the agencies get the money.
The president requested $541 million for the Federal Emergency Management Agency to address emergency needs arising from recent severe winter storms in the west.

He also asked for another $438 million in contingent funding for the agency, to be made available for emergency needs as they become known, including damage estimates from the recent tornadoes in Arkansas.
Other funding sought by Clinton included $276 million for the Federal Highway Administration to repair highway damage resulting from floods.
The Ohio River valley was pummeled in February and March by rains and deadly floods, and government experts say more flooding could be on the way this spring.

Clinton asked for $240.7 million for the Corps of Engineers, most of which would be used to repair damaged levees and to dredge harbours damaged by floods, plus another $50 million in contingent funding for potential spring flooding.

Clinton asked for $213.4 million for the Department of the Interior. Much of this would go to the National Park Serice to repair and replace facilities at 10 national parks, including Yosemite National Park which was damaged by winter storms.
Clinton asked for $126.1 million for the Department of Agriculture to help with soil erosion and other problems faced by farmers and ranchers whose land was damaged by flooding.
He sought $22.8 million for the Commerce Department so that its National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration can repair damage to fish hatcheries and restore other fish habitats in the West.
